title: MAG-S3, MAG-S3b and MAG-S3c: recording the quantum compass, CISS non-reciprocity, cryptochrome order and real pair geometry
description: Release v0.3.2 makes four wording fixes to the notes after release of MAG-S3c: an oriented sample reads the whole odd dipole only if all its molecules share one orientation and the field probes all three directions; the check Q1 covers the numerics of the harmonics and leaves open whether the transfer to the neural code holds; the bounds of the invariants I10 and I11 are rounded up; and the relaxation levels of the cells after release are named. The numbers, the frozen protocol, code, run and verdicts are those of v0.3.1 (10.5281/zenodo.24157274). Release v0.3.1 added notes after release to MAG-S3c (section "Notes after release" of mag_s3c/README.md and of the protocol with results). Read with the definition of Kobori et al. (2026), CISS efficiency 100(1 − cos χ) for the singlet-born state cos(χ/2)|S⟩ + sin(χ/2)|T₀⟩, their 6% for the pair FAD–W_C is χ = 20°, and their model recombines at −χ, the form P-LH of MAG-S3c, with the CISS axis along the pair axis; the fitted angles come from the cryptochrome-DASH of Xenopus laevis and serve as a parameter scenario for Cry4. At their angles and at the Cry4a rates of the run, P-LH gives an odd part 2.4–4.5 times below the threshold of the dipole test along the pair axis in W_C by the stricter transfer (0.024–0.026 by the ratio transfer), while the coherence form K at the same triplet population stays about 3 times above it in W_C and 9–11 times in W_D, and P-0 and P-same stay visible; at fast recombination (branch E12), closer to the kinetics of Kobori et al., P-LH lies 13–130 times above the threshold without relaxation. This withdraws the statement of v0.3.0 that the W_C pair stands at the threshold at their scale. The exchange coupling they fitted, J = 22 μT, changes P-LH by 5–17% and lowers the response of P-same in W_C by a factor of 1.7–2.6. The half-rate of 3.3–6.2e7 per second belongs to the projection of the odd dipole on the receptor axis; its full length, which dephasing also turns, halves at 4.5–6.7e7 per second or above 1e8 in W_C and above 1e8 in W_D. The frozen protocol, code, run and verdicts are those of v0.3.0 (10.5281/zenodo.24148799). Release v0.3.0 added MAG-S3c (folder mag_s3c). MAG-S3c is a pre-registered simulation study of whether the two main conclusions of MAG-S3b survive the real geometry of the radical pair in cryptochrome 4 and spin relaxation, and how much of the odd part of the compass code, the part that changes sign when the field is reversed, the singlet–triplet coherence itself carries. It recomputes the three-nucleus radical pair of MAG-S3b in three geometries: the tensors of MAG-S2, and the FAD–W_C (W318) and FAD–W_D (W369) pairs of pigeon cryptochrome 4 (ClCry4a, PDB 6PU0) with their point-dipole coupling (0.34 and 0.19 mT), with singlet–triplet dephasing up to 1e8 per second, beyond the 3–6e7 per second that Golesworthy et al. (2023) estimated from experiments on modified Cry4a, and random fields up to 3e7 per second. Five hypotheses get a verdict per geometry from 184 comparisons; exploratory maps add the microscopic CISS form of Denton et al. (2026), fast recombination, the composite pair W_C–W_D with hops of the hole, the sphere of CISS axes, the receptor axis and the average over the P2₁2₁2₁ crystal packing of 6PU0 (point group 222). The protocol (v0.4, in Russian), code, structure file, reference calibration and Colab notebook were frozen on 10 November 2026 at 19:40 UTC and their SHA-256 posted in Telegram (https://t.me/attractordm/79) no later than 19:42 UTC, the minute the run started. The confirmatory run of 10–11 November 2026 was continued in parts of 1.5 h after parts of 0.5 h stopped the slowest cells at every pause, a deviation recorded before the continuation (mag_s3c/results/run_notes.md). The run is valid: all eleven invariants held, and a reanalysis of the archive reproduced every value of the results bit for bit. The odd dipole follows the hyperfine tensors: in the real pairs its projection on the receptor axis for CISS axes across the receptor is 3.3–4.0 times its value for the axis along the flavin normal (H2 met). The singlet–triplet coherence creates it, with a share of at least 0.975 (H5 met), and relaxation at 1e6 per second keeps at least 79% of it (H4 met). Its projection on the receptor axis falls by half at a dephasing rate of 3.3–6.2e7 per second in the real pairs (above 1e8 for one axis), inside the estimated 3–6e7 per second or above it and never below, although at 6e7 per second less than half of it remains in 8 of the 12 combinations of the real pairs; random fields halve it at 2.7–7.9e6 per second. The dipole test sees both candidate pairs at a non-reciprocity of 0.1 pi along the transfer path with a margin of 5–18 times by the stricter transfer (H3 met). H3 was not met in the sealed verdict line of a trial run at substitute rates before the freeze; the line was opened after the run, its SHA-256 matched the published one, and an exploratory recomputation attributes the difference to the 60-direction grid of the trial. Both CISS forms carry singlet–triplet coherence, imaginary in the coherence form and real, which means opposite polarisations of the two spins, in the polarisation forms. The dominance of the coherence form of CISS over the polarisation forms holds only without the dipolar coupling (H1 met in the MAG-S2 geometry, not met in W_C and W_D): in the real pairs the polarisation form gives an odd part 3–40 times larger than the coherence form in the molecular measure, and at zero dipolar coupling the coherence form is again 68–4200 times stronger. A null result of the reference recording therefore limits polarisation at birth too. At the CISS scale of Kobori et al. (2026), read with their definition as described above, visibility to the dipole test depends on how CISS enters recombination and on how fast the pair recombines. Hopping between W_C and W_D with recombination at both sites gives an odd part without CISS comparable to that of CISS, and the crystal 6PU0 cancels the dipolar part of the odd pattern. All numbers belong to three nitrogen nuclei, J = 0 and isotropic models of relaxation. The MAG-S3 and MAG-S3b files, runs and verdicts are those of releases v0.1.1 (10.5281/zenodo.24044654), v0.2.0 (10.5281/zenodo.24079875) and v0.2.1 (10.5281/zenodo.24100330) and are unchanged.
